headline: Approved new Strategy and Communication Lead position 4-3, and FY '27 budget transfers except Lawrence School request.
summary: Residents spoke about the lack of a contract for the secretaries' association, which has worked 479 days without one. Principals presented school improvement plans for MacArthur, Stanley, and Waltham High. Assistant Superintendent Chad Mazza's contract was amended to end October 31, 2026.
decisions: Approved consent agenda items B-E, all in favor.
Approved minutes of the October 7, 2026 regular meeting, 5-0 with one abstention.
Approved staff out-of-district request for the 2026-2027 school year.
Approved addition of a Strategy and Communication Lead position to the district, 4-3.
Approved amendment to Chad Mazza's contract with an end date of October 31, 2026, 5-1.
Approved Mayor McCarthy executing the FY '26 School Department End of Year Report Certification.
Tabled the 617 Transformer Project until the next meeting.
Approved paying the bills on the warrant.
Approved FY '27 budget transfer requests except the request for the Lawrence School.

WALTHAM SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
 Waltham, Massachusetts 
 MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING  OCTOBER 21, 2026 
 RECESS 
 RECONVENE 
 PUBLIC INPUT 
 The regular meeting of the Waltham School Committee convened at 5:34pm. Present 
 were Ms. Wong-Bigelow, Ms. DeJoannis, Mrs. AlJammal, Mrs. Coleman, and Mr. 
 Zanghi.  Mr. Tarallo and Mayor McCarthy were not present.  Mrs. Coleman presided. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. AlJammal, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to move to 
 Executive Session at 5:34pm to conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective 
 bargaining with the WSSA and / or to conduct negotiations with the WSSA; to 
 conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective bargaining with the WSAA and / 
 or to conduct negotiations with the WSAA; to conduct strategy sessions with respect 
 to collective bargaining with the Waltham School MIS Technicians and / or to conduct 
 negotiations with the Waltham School MIS Technicians; to conduct strategy sessions 
 with respect to collective bargaining with the Waltham School Department Food 
 Service Workers; to conduct strategy sessions in preparation for negotiations with 
 nonunion personnel and/or to conduct negotiations with nonunion personnel  – 
 Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations; to conduct strategy sessions 
 with respect to collective bargaining with the Waltham Building Maintenance Workers 
 Association and/or to conduct negotiations with the Waltham Building Maintenance 
 Workers Association; in accordance with Mass. G.L. c. 30A, Section 21(a)(3), to 
 discuss strategy with respect to litigation if an open meeting may have a detrimental 
 effect on the litigating position of the public body and the chair so declares - Waltham 
 School Secretaries Association and the Waltham Public Schools MUP-26-12223, and 
 In accordance with Mass. G.L. c. 30A, Section 21(a)(3), to discuss strategy with 
 respect to litigation if an open meeting may have a detrimental effect on the litigating 
 position of the public body and the chair so declares - Waltham School Secretaries 
 Association and the Waltham School Committee MUP-26-12365, to include Attorney 
 Jonathan Atwater, HR Administrator Kate Peretz and Superintendent Dr. Mendonsa, 
 and return to the regular meeting at 7:00 pm.  All in favor. 
 The School Committee reconvened at 7:04pm.  Present were Mr. Tarallo, Mr. Zanghi, 
 Mrs. Coleman, Mrs. AlJammal, Ms. DeJoannis, Ms. Wong-Bigelow, and Mayor 
 McCarthy.  Mayor McCarthy presided. 
 The Committee recited the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 The Mayor confirmed the meeting was being recorded by  WCAC.org  .  No one in 
 attendance indicated they were recording the meeting. 
 Waltham School Secretaries Association President Kris Scheufele and members 
 Karen Lawn and Mary Jo Nash expressed their frustration with the lack of contract for 
 the WSSA.  They stated they have continued to work 479 days and have not 
 received a fair and equitable contract offer from the School Committee.  Ms. 
 Scheufele referenced budget decisions made, the FY ‘26 deficit, and higher salary 
 amounts offered to new staff.  They urged the Committee to settle with the unions 
 that continue to work without a contract before new positions are added to the 
 district. 
 Nicole Piche-Nicholas and Tricia Hurley, both Waltham High School parents, 
 emphasized the importance of sharing all schedule options with the community

 before decisions are made that eliminate possibilities.  They requested transparency 
 in the process, visibility into the schedule options being considered, data and 
 evidence being analyzed, and how the options will impact students within CTE, 
 Special Education and English Learners. 
 WPS parent, Eric Hoffman, referenced the recent altercation between students at 
 Kennedy and asked the Committee members if staff should intervene in future 
 situations.  He added that staff training protects both students and staff and 
 requested that the district’s expectation of teachers in these situations be 
 communicated to the community. 
 There were no students in attendance at the meeting. 
 There was no one present from these groups.

 The superintendent shared two generous donations from Watertown Savings Bank: 
 ●  A donation in the amount of $3,000. to the Waltham High School Golf Team; 
 ●  A donation in the amount of $1,500 to Waltham High School’s Girls Soccer 
 Team 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to approve items 
 B-E on the Consent Agenda.  All in favor.

 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to approve the 
 Minutes from the Regular Meeting held on October 7, 2026.  Roll call  :  Mr. Zanghi - 
 yes; Mr. Tarallo - yes; Mrs. AlJammal  - yes; Ms. DeJoannis  - yes; Ms. Wong-Bigelow 
 - yes, and Mrs. Coleman - abstain. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Mrs.  AlJammal, to approve the 
 staff out of district request for the 2026-2027 school year.  All in favor. 
 New Hires: 
 ●  Karin Knudson, LTS Math Teacher, Waltham High School - effective

 ●  Mariaelisa Castillo, School Psychologist, District-Wide - effective 10/08/2026;

 All district staff and families were sent a calendar survey with questions about the 
 2027-2028 school year.  The survey is open through October 30, 2026 and results 
 will be shared with the Committee in November. 
 Waltham High Senior Leah France was named the #MakeMercyReal Tik Tok 
 Challenge winner and was awarded a full four year free ride by Saint Joseph’s 
 College in Maine.  France was recognized for her dedication to inclusivity and 
 disability advocacy for her involvement in programs such as Best Buddies and WHS’ 
 Unified Basketball team. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to hear from all 
 off-Committee members.  All in favor. 
 From the area of Curriculum and Instruction, Director Matt Burns and Teacher Anna 
 Davtian shared updates from the science department.  At the elementary schools, 
 information was shared about STEM work, professional development, and support 
 and expectations for teachers.  At the middle and high schools, OpenSciEd is being 
 used at Kennedy and McDevitt and in physics, chemistry and biology at Waltham 
 High.  Project Lead the Way (PLTW) is expanding at the middle school level and 
 Valor students are receiving hands-on biology and engineering support. 
 Mayor McCarthy asked Mr. Burns to confirm if his role includes providing professional 
 development for his staff and handling evaluations and he acknowledged both as part 
 of his position.

 a)  School

 ____________________________  -4-  OCTOBER 21  , 2026 
 Dr. Lisa Kingsley shared some of the main focuses of the department: the migration 
 to Lilypad to handle tracking of IEPs and 504 plans, targeted professional 
 development to help align staff workflows to school standards, and stronger oversight 
 of annual IEP reviews and three-year reevaluations. 
 Multiple questions were asked by the Committee about Lilypad’s capacity to work 
 with Aspen, 504 plans, and translation and Dr. Kingsley answered these. 
 Within the Human Resources Department, Ms. Peretz indicated that the addition of a 
 new staff member will allow for the shift of additional tasks into the HR office.  Work 
 continues to recruit and retain diverse staff, to expand new higher education 
 partnerships, and to advance RTAP. 
 Dr. Ray Porch provided information about school site councils: the purpose, 
 responsibilities, membership, elections, and meeting procedures.  Questions about 
 site council elections, terms, hospitality, discussion items, training, and the site 
 council document were all addressed by Dr. Porch. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to hear from 
 off-committee members.  All in favor. 
 MacArthur Elementary School Principal Kevin Kmiec and Assistant Principal Rob 
 Howes shared insight into the development of the school’s plan.  Some goals mirror 
 last year’s because continued progress in these essential areas is important. 
 MacArthur’s Student Learning goal was identified as, “MacArthur students will 
 increase their written expression skills from the Fall 2026 Assessment to the Spring 
 2027 assessment as measured by the MacArthur Baseline benchmark writing 
 assessments and curriculum-based writing assessments using the Informative/ 
 Explanatory Writing Rubric from the ELA Massachusetts Curriculum Frameworks.” 
 The school’s Professional Practice goal is “MacArthur Staff will increase their 
 knowledge of the core elements of the pedagogical practice in the Bridges in 
 Mathematics program related to increasing student voice and ownership in class 
 discussions. As a result of this work, MacArthur teachers will develop a deep 
 understanding of the instructional shifts of this core resource and apply the lessons 
 with a data driven focus.” 
 The principal  advised the School Learning Culture goal has been established as 
 “MacArthur Faculty and Staff will enhance the learning culture of MacArthur School 
 through the consistent application of school wide practices related to our core values. 
 This includes the development of Tier 1 learning opportunities focused on improving 
 the growth mindset of all learners. As a result, MacArthur students will increase their 
 school readiness and ability to persevere through learning tasks.” 
 Information as to the school’s plan to achieve these goals and monitor progress was 
 explained. The members took turns asking questions of Mr. Kmiec and Mr. Howes 
 and sharing their appreciation of their work. 
 Mrs. Coleman left the meeting at 9:00pm and returned at 9:05pm.

 ____________________________  -5-  OCTOBER 21  , 2026 
 Stanley Elementary’s Principal Jennifer Hacker, accompanied by Assistant Principal 
 Erika Walther, advised their goals are intertwined and reflect similarities to last year’s. 
 They emphasized the importance of educating the whole student. 
 The school’s Student Learning goal was identified as “During the 2026–2027 school 
 year, 100% of students will articulate and demonstrate mastery of daily learning 
 objectives in literacy and math, resulting in at least 80% of students meeting 
 grade-level benchmarks on common assessments, with 100% of high-risk students 
 and English Learners making accelerated growth through co-taught inclusive 
 instruction.” 
 Stanley’s Professional Practice goal for this year is, “During the 2026–2027 school 
 year, 100% of teaching staff will design and post clear, measurable daily learning 
 objectives and collaboratively plan and deliver Tier 1 instruction using flexible 
 co-teaching models, resulting in at least 75% of students meeting grade-level 
 benchmarks on literacy and math assessments and a 25% reduction in students 
 requiring high-risk Tier 2/3 interventions, ensuring 100% of at-risk students and 
 multilingual learners receive scaffolded, inclusive instruction.” 
 Mrs. Hacker advised the School Culture goal is, “By June 2027, 100% of Stanley staff 
 will participate in CPT and data cycle team meetings focused on shared student data 
 and collaborative intervention planning, resulting in a 15% increase in staff 
 agreement on the annual culture survey regarding "shared responsibility for student 
 success," while systematically identifying and implementing equitable academic and 
 behavioral supports that reduce the school's grade-level achievement gap by 10%.” 
 The principal explained the plan to achieve each of the goals along with the data that 
 will be tracked to monitor progress.  Mrs. Hacker answered questions and received 
 very positive feedback from the members. 
 Waltham High School’s principal, Bill Conard, shared his thoughts on his new 
 position and the start to the year.  He explained that given the school’s accountability 
 rating, DESE required the detailed school improvement plan to be submitted last 
 spring. 
 Waltham High’s Student Learning goal for this year is, “By June 2027, classrooms 
 across all grades and subject areas will pilot and implement High-Quality 
 Instructional Materials (HQIM) and/or protocols to support disciplinary literacy. This 
 will result in at least a 5% increase in students meeting or exceeding proficiency 
 targets on standards-aligned assessments.” 
 The school’s Professional Practice goal has been set as, “Throughout the 2026–2027 
 school year, instructional staff will actively participate in weekly, protocol-driven 
 Common Planning Time (CPT) and building meetings to engage in professional 
 development, analyze live student data, adjust future planning, and implement 
 interventions.” 
 The School Culture goal is, “By June 2027, Waltham High School will increase the 
 overall student attendance rate from 93% to 95%, reduce chronic absenteeism 
 across all subgroups by at least 15%, and decrease the annual school-wide dropout 
 rate to below 3.0%.”

 The Committee welcomed Dr. Conard and engaged him in discussions about the 
 goals and plans to inspire students to stay engaged in learning. 
 Nothing new was shared in this area. 
 Dr. Mendonsa advised she has a meeting scheduled with SMMA next week to 
 discuss the possible renovation options for the 617 Lexington Street building. 
 There was no new information shared in this area. 
 The superintendent confirmed an update was shared with the whole WPS community 
 today and identified dates in November in which forums will be held with staff, 
 students and families to review the proposed schedule models.  While no single 
 schedule will fit for every student, the proposed models will take into consideration 
 students in general education, CTE, Special Education, and English learners, and will 
 identify successes and barriers within each. 
 There was nothing new discussed within this category. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to table this item 
 to the next meeting.  All in favor. 
 Mayor McCarthy advised the School Committee’s policy manual is available online 
 and includes the district’s policy on physical restraint. 
 Dr. Mendonsa explained her belief that repurposing a prior position to create a new 
 role that will handle strategy and communication for the district, in addition to being 
 the DEI point-person, is much needed at this time.  Mr. Tarallo and Mrs. Coleman 
 spoke in support of the position citing the importance of communication to our 
 community.  Mayor McCarthy explained her disagreement with the addition of this 
 new position at this time, especially given the comments made during Public Input.

 Ms. Wong-Bigelow - yes; Ms. DeJoannis - no; Mrs. AlJammal - yes; Mr. Tarallo - yes; 
 Mr. Zanghi - no; Mayor McCarthy - no, and Mrs. Coleman - yes. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Mr.  Tarallo, to amend the 
 Contract of Employment between Waltham Public Schools and Chad Mazza, for the 
 position of Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations, to include a 
 contract end date of October 31, 2026.  Roll call:  Ms. Wong-Bigelow - yes; Ms. 
 DeJoannis - yes; Mrs. AlJammal - yes; Mrs. Coleman - yes; Mr. Tarallo - yes, and Mr.

 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to approve

 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Ms.  DeJoannis, to table this 
 matter to the next meeting.  All in favor. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Mr.  Tarallo, to move item 10d out 
 of order.  All in favor. 
 Mr. Tarallo requested more information be made available on the warrants that are 
 presented for approval at each meeting.  A short conversation with the Mayor 
 ensued. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mrs.  Coleman, to pay the bills on the 
 warrant.  All in favor. 
 The superintendent advised the intent of her transfer requests is to resolve deficits 
 which exist in some of the accounts due to expenses already incurred within the first 
 quarter of the fiscal year.  Mrs. AlJammal questioned the Lawrence School expense 
 and Mayor McCarthy confirmed she will look into that matter as the School 
 Department previously transferred care, custody and control back to the city.
